rv.q: Not the whole time, but smile at these mostly young, talented singers you will.
Their production of A Little Night Music is a complete joy and one of the best I can ever recall seeing.
My advice: Catch this production if you can.

Visiting from Mercury Theater, L. Walter Stearns certainly brings the light-comedy whipped cream (and Brenda Didier keeps everyone swirling in waltz time), but he also ensures that those knives poke as sharply as they have to.

Theo Ubique Cabaret Theatre offers a perfect way to experience this sophisticated 1973 farce—in a small, intimate setting with a fine, four-piece band and a talented cast that can handle both the wit of Hugh Wheeler’s book and the difficulty of Sondheim’s score.
Ms. Kessel brings just the proper emotional commitment to the role, as she provides devotion, affection and encouragement to Jesus.
This is a show that you should put on your "to do" list, and actually do it!
Stephen Soundheim’s classic A Little Night Music (ALNM) at Theo Ubique is a divine gift to its audience, as it is a beautiful and genuine production worthy of not missing.
